newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian PZ full year profits cheer market.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian PZ full year profits cheer market.

text.p: An increase in full year profits at Nigerian conglomerate PZ Industries, which the company attributed to long term investment, cheered share traders on Friday.
After-tax profit almost doubled for the year at 1,380 million naira to May 30 1996, from 796 million naira the year before.
"We are reaping the reward of our investment over the years, and we have invested quite heavily," Kola Jamodu, chief executive officer, told Reuters.
He said profits were up in line with a big increase in turnover, rising to 13.98 billion naira from 8.07 billion naira in 1995.
On the Nigerian stock exchange traders reacted favourably to the result, saying it was consistent with their expectations.
"Based on their half-year and nine-month results, I would say that it was in line with the market's expectation" trader James Odife of Centre-Point Investments said.
He said the company's performance could be due to good management policy.
Jamodu did not say which of its products accounted most for the profits but said PZ was the market leader in soaps and detergents.
"We are also quality conscious and consumer oriented," he added.

Besides a dividend per share of 30 kobo, the company is proposing a scrip issue of one new share for every four held in February 1997 on completion of a proposed merger with associate Thermocool Engineering Company.

Its share price was unchanged at 36.00 naira because of a technical suspension due to the announcement of the impending merger but one trader said the share price would be likely to take off as soon as dealing became possible.
PZ Industries Nigeria is at least 40 percent owned by Britain's Paterson Zochonis Plc.
